title: Composed characters get queued over time in Ubuntu
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in: 4.6.2.stable, 4.7.beta, 4.7.2.rc1, 4.8.dev2

### System information

Godot v4.7.2.rc1 - Ubuntu 26.04 LTS 26.04 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Mobile) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 (nvidia; 580.173.02) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-14900K (32 threads) - 14.79 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono)

### Issue description

When writing in a TextExit node while using the Compose Key to form characters like "é" and "ã", over time the character gets stored instead of written. Later on this causes an issue where if you write "é" and then "á" later, the "é" might get queued and be typed instead of "á" when the Compose Key is used to form any other character. It's not limited to storing one character, as during my testing I've been able to have a delay of three Compose characters.
The queue gets cleared if I rerun the project. It only exists within Godot, other applications are unaffected.
I can see this as maybe being an Ubuntu issue as it is fixed if I execute in the terminal:
```
ibus restart
```
Which will work for any subsequent runs of any projects which may have a TextEdit node, and there won't be a queue anymore up until the system is restarted. Only consequence is there won't be a preview of the Compose characters until the resulting character is typed.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Have a TextEdit node in a scene, and run the scene
2. Continuously use the Compose Key to form different characters

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A
